_comment: Industry config for licensed electrical contractors.
rsa_guidance: Lead with safety, licensed/bonded/insured, code compliance, and permit-pulled work. Electrical work has high perceived risk — credentials and safety messaging are the top conversion levers. Urgency is relevant for electrical emergencies (no power, sparking outlets, burning smell).

city.heading: Electrical Problems Are a Safety Issue — Don't Wait
city.intro: Faulty wiring and electrical faults are the leading cause of house fires in the US. What looks like a minor issue — a flickering light, a warm outlet — can be a serious hazard. Licensed electricians catch these before they become emergencies.
bullets: Sparking or warm outlets: a sign of loose connections or overloaded circuits
Flickering lights: often indicates wiring issues or a failing panel
Burning smell near outlets: a fire hazard — turn off the breaker and call immediately
Tripping breakers: repeated trips mean the circuit is overloaded or there's a fault

cost.heading: What Does {service} Cost?
cost.intro: Electrical costs vary by job complexity, panel size, and whether permits are required. We provide a written upfront quote before any work starts — no surprise invoices.
bullets: Panel upgrades: cost depends on amp capacity and whether new wiring runs are needed
Permits: we pull all required permits — factored into the quote upfront
Code compliance: older homes often need code updates alongside the primary job
EV chargers and generators: eligible for federal and state tax credits that reduce net cost
cost.callout: We provide a written upfront estimate before any work begins. Permits included, no hidden fees.

company.heading: Why Choose Us?
company.intro: Electrical work is not the place to cut corners. Here's why homeowners and businesses trust us.
bullets: Licensed & Bonded: fully licensed electrical contractor — license number available on request
Insured: general liability and workers' comp on every job
Code-Compliant: all work meets or exceeds local and national electrical code (NEC)
Permit-Pulled: we handle all permits so your work is on record and your insurance stays valid

free-estimate.heading: What Happens During a Free Estimate?
free-estimate.intro: Our licensed electricians assess the job on-site and give you a written quote before any work starts. No obligation, no pressure.
bullets: We inspect the area and identify all work required — no hidden scope
We check for code compliance issues that may affect the job
We explain permit requirements and factor them into the quote
You get a written estimate with a clear breakdown — decide on your own timeline
free-estimate.callout: The estimate is completely free. If you move forward, most jobs can be scheduled within 1–2 days.

insurance.heading: Does Insurance Cover Electrical Repairs?
insurance.intro: Homeowner's insurance typically covers electrical damage caused by a covered event (fire, storm, power surge). Work done without a permit may void your coverage — we always pull permits.
bullets: Storm damage: lightning-related electrical damage is usually covered under homeowner's policies
Fire damage: electrical fire repair is typically covered — we document the damage for your adjuster
Permit records: all our work is on record, which protects your insurance coverage
Tax credits: EV charger and solar installations may qualify for federal tax credits
insurance.callout: Ask us about documentation for your insurance claim — we provide the report your adjuster needs.

removal.heading: How {service} Works
removal.intro: Our licensed electricians follow a code-compliant process from assessment to final inspection.
bullets: On-site assessment — evaluate existing wiring, panel capacity, and permit requirements
Written quote — itemized breakdown before any work starts
Permit pulled — filed with the local authority before work begins
Installation — code-compliant work by licensed electricians
Inspection — we coordinate the final inspection with the local authority
Sign-off — permit closed, work is on record
